senses.gloss: to go out, come out; to result, end. Targ. O. VIII, 7 מִיפַּק ed. Berl. (oth. ed. a. Y. מֵיפַק); a. v. fr.—Y. Ber. I, 2ᶜ top שרי מלכא נ׳ וכ׳ when the king begins to march out, even if he has not yet gone out, we say, he has gone out. Ib. 3ᶜ bot. הוינן נַפְקִין לתעניתא we went out for fast and prayer.
units: <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 10:8:1">Koh. R. to X, 8</cite> <he>מִינְּפַק ליה</he> (= <he>מן נ׳</he>) after he came out.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Taanit 4:5:15">Y. Taan. IV, 69ᵃ</cite> <he>מִנַּפְקִין</he> when they came out; <cite ref="Eichah Rabbah 2">Lam. R. to II, 2</cite> <he>מן דנַפְקוּן</he>. Y. l. c. <he>לא נפקון טבאות</he> (Matt. K. to Lam. R. l. c. <he>לא נַפְקַת להון</he>) they did not end well. Pesik. B’shall., p. 94ᵃ <he>וגוש חלבאי נפקין וכ׳</he> and the men of Giscala went out after them with sticks &c.; <cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 11:2">Koh. R. to XI, 2</cite> <he>וגוש חלב אנפקין</he> (corr. acc.); a. v. fr.—Imperat. <cite ref="Q00314"><he>פּוּק</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 8:16">Targ. Gen. VIII, 16</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Eruvin 14b">Erub. 14ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>פ׳ חזי וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="D00076"><he>דְּבַר</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Shabbat 106a">Sabb. 106ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>פ׳ תני וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="B01153"><he>בַּר</he></cite> I ch.—Part. <cite ref="N01047"><he>נָפֵיק</he></cite>.
Targ. I Kings XV, 17; v. next w.; a. fr.—(כנ׳) כד נפיק ביה = h. כיוצא בו (v. יָצָא) similar to, corresponding.
<cite ref="Targum Jerusalem, Genesis 2:18">Targ. Y. II, Gen. II, 18</cite>.

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Deuteronomy 14:8">Targ. Y. Deut. XIV, 8</cite> (not <he>כַּנְפֵיק</he>, <he>כַּנְפַק</he>).—Y. Ber. VI, 10ᵇ bot. <he>נ׳ אנא ידי חובתי</he> do I do my duty?, v. <cite ref="J00515"><he>יָצָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Sukkah 36b:3">Succ. 36ᵇ</cite> <he>ונ׳ בה</he> and used it for doing his duty (for the ceremony of Ethrog).—

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 6:2:2">Y. Sabb. VI, 8ᵃ</cite> top, a. e. <he>מה נָ׳ מן ביניהון</he> what is the outcome from between them?, i.e. what is the difference between them in practice?—<he>נפקא מינה וכ׳</he> the practical difference is &c.

<cite ref="Beitzah 6b:12">Bets. 6ᵇ</cite> <he>למאי נ׳ מינה</he> in regard to what practice is there a difference (whether or not eggs found in a chicken can be hatched)? <he>למקח וממכר</he> it makes a difference in trade (if one bought eggs for breeding).
<cite ref="Ketubot 72a:6">Keth. 72ᵃ</cite> <he>מאי נ׳ לה מינה תיעביד</he> what difference does it make to her? let her do it; a. v. fr.—
<cite ref="Temurah 7a:9">Tem. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>נ׳ ליה וכ׳</he> it is derived from the Biblical word &c.
<cite ref="Temurah 7a:23">Ib.</cite> <he>תֵּיפוּק ליה זריקה וכ׳</he> let ‘sprinkling’ be derived from &c.—
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 52">Gen. R. s. 52</cite> <he>ונֵיפוֹק ידוי</he> and do justice to it (to the verse to be explained), v. supra.
<cite ref="Shabbat 74a:1">Sabb. 74ᵃ</cite> <he>ולֵיפוּק חדא וכ׳</he> let him take out one (of the enumerated categories) and insert another one.
<cite ref="Chullin 43a:1">Ḥull. 43ᵃ</cite> <he>לא תִיפַּק</he>, v. infra.—[<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Amos 9:13">Targ. Am. IX, 13</cite>, v. infra.]

senses.gloss: to lead forth, carry forth; to bring forth, produce; to derive; to take out, exclude.
units: <cite ref="Onkelos Exodus 16:3">Targ. Ex. XVI, 3</cite>.
<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Amos 9:13">Targ. Am. IX, 13</cite> <he>במַפִּיק</he> ed. Lag. (oth. ed. <he>במִפַּק</he>, corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 15:13">Targ. Job XV, 13</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Berakhot 38a">Ber. 38ᵃ</cite> (ref. to <he>המוציא</he> in the benediction over bread) <he>דא׳ משמע</he> it means ‘who has brought forth’; <he>דמַפִּיק משמע</he> it means ‘who brings forth’.
<cite ref="Berakhot 38a">Ib.</cite> <he>אַפִּיקוּ ליה ריפתא</he> they brought out bread (and placed it) before him.

<cite ref="Berakhot 38a">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <he>המוציא</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 6:7">Ex. VI, 7</cite>) <he>כד מַפִּיקְנָא לכו … דאַפֵּיקִית וכ׳</he> when I lead you forth, I shall do for you a thing that you may know that it is I who led you forth.
<cite ref="Sotah 16b">Sot. 16ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 13a:4">R. Hash. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>לא תַפִּיק נפשך יכ׳</he> do not let thyself go beyond the established rule.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 60a:11">B. Bath. 60ᵃ</cite> <he>דהוה מַפִּיק וכ׳</he> which led to (opened towards) etc.
<cite ref="Temurah 3b:72">Tem. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>מפיק שם וכ׳</he> utters the name of the Lord in vain.
<cite ref="Temurah 7a:25">Ib. 7ᵃ</cite> <he>מַפְּקִינָן לבמת יחיד</he> we derive from it a rule for individual high-places.—
<cite ref="Chullin 42b:4">Ḥull. 42ᵇ</cite> <he>אַפֵּיק חדא וכ׳</he> take out one category and insert another.
Ib. 43ᵃ top הנך דאַפְּקַת לא תַפִּיק Tosaf. (ed. לא תיפק) the two which thou didst exclude, do not exclude; a. v. fr.—לְאַפּוּקֵי or לַאֲפוּקֵי to the exclusion of, v. אַפֵּק.

senses.gloss: to take out by legal decision; to collect; to claim.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 76b:1">Keth. 76ᵇ</cite> <he>מייתי אב ראיה ומפיק</he> the father brings evidence and gets a verdict for collecting, opp. <he>ומוקים</he> for letting the money stand where it is. Y. Gitt. I, end, 43ᵈ <he>ואַפְּקוּן מיניה</he> and collected from him.
Ib. בעון מִיפְּקָא (v. supra Pe. 2) they wanted to collect. Y. Shebu. VII, 38ᵃ top אתון ואַפְּקוּן דלא וכ׳ they came and claimed that he had not given them anything; a. fr.
<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 38:25">Targ. Gen. XXXVIII, 25</cite>; a. fr.—Y. Gitt. VI, 48ᵃ bot. <he>אתא׳ למקטלא</he> was led out to be executed.
